content:
Hi, I'm trying to use Verso to document my project.

I copied verso-templates/package-docs/manual to a subdirectory of my project, and changed Docs.lean as follows (as well as commenting out everything that referred to Zippers).

set_option verso.exampleProject ".."
set_option verso.exampleModule "Fun.Logic" -- my project has a file Fun/Logic.lean

lake exe docs in the manual directory produces this opaque error:

error: Docs.lean:43:55: Build process failed.
CWD: ..
Command: elan
Args: #["run", "--install", "leanprover/lean4:v4.29.0", "lake", "build", "subverso-extract-mod"]
Exit code: 1
stdout:
stderr: error: unknown target `subverso-extract-mod`

The lean-toolchain versions are the same, v4.29.0.
I've tried a bunch of things, like trying to remove unnecessary files from the manual directory, or making manual a sibling directory, but I don't know enough about how all this is implemented to understand the error.

What am I doing wrong? Is this the way Verso is intended to be used, with a subdirectory? Can I just include Verso in my lakefile.toml and use it that way?

Cannot reproduce.

The error means that Lake did not find the build target subverso-extract-mod. Are you able to build the manual inside the "full" template (i.e. without any modifications)?

discuss9128 said:

Is this the way Verso is intended to be used, with a subdirectory? Can I just include Verso in my lakefile.toml and use it that way?

Yes, this is the intended way. In particular it is desirable to uncouple the Lean version used for the actual code and for the manual, for instance if new versions of Verso require a more recent compiler and you want to make use of those features without updating the Lean version of your project. (This is explained in the Docs.lean file of the template you are using.)

It is possible to manage everything from a single lakefile.toml, but as explained above this might be undesirable. In any case that requires some rudimentary understanding of Lean's build system.

Thanks for your reply. I narrowed the problem down and found that I had missed including a dependency on subverso in the main project. Now everything works!

I guess having subverso included in the main project is what allows the versions to be decoupled, as it allows for negotiation between the versions.

I see. Indeed, one can find the following:

The example project must depend on the same version of subverso that the document's Verso version uses.

https://github.com/leanprover/verso-templates/blob/be22df1b674b0f7b69b76a81fe4c68166c62af07/package-docs/manual/Docs/DocFeatures.lean#L32

Perhaps this should be advertised more explicitly in the readme file of the template.
Ah, yes. Perhaps just a one-liner saying how a prospective user would build the manual for their project, before pointing them to the Verso files.
